transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-28 10:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Connor, Priya Sharma, Diego Alvarez, Hannah Lee + company all-hands (open)

Summary: quick roadmap / hiring / pricing / reliability decision sprint

[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Okay thanks everyone for joining the Crestview sprint, uh we're trying to keep this tight, 60 minutes, focused decisions. I'll kick off with the framing.
[00:00:12] Liam O'Connor: Quick housekeeping - sharing screen in a sec - the deck has three possible hiring bundles: Growth, Product, Infra. We want to lock a provisional one today.
[00:00:28] Priya Sharma: I have one ask up front, like if we go with infra hires we need time to ramp and a clear set of objectives. Can't just throw heads at problems.
[00:00:41] Hannah Lee: From finance perspective the runway with current ARR but unchanged pricing puts pressure in Q4; we can afford 3 net new roles in the ramp window without changing forecasts.
[00:00:55] Diego Alvarez: Also research needs two engineers to onboard the new KV-cache experiments—without them model latency regression risk increases.

[00:01:10] Maya Chen: Noted. Agenda: 1) hiring bundle 2) Dedicated pricing sensitivity 3) latency SLO targets 4) audit/regulatory timeline. We'll go in that order.

-- Hiring bundle discussion --
[00:01:35] Liam O'Connor: Slide 4 shows three cohorts. Bundle A: 2 infra, 1 SE, 1 PM. Bundle B: 1 infra, 2 product, 2 growth. Bundle C: conservative single hire. My ask is we pick A or B.
[00:01:55] Hannah Lee: Financially, A is the highest burn but has the best short-term reliability upside for Dedicated. B supports growth and feature velocity.
[00:02:12] Priya Sharma: If we prioritize Dedicated performance, infra hires accelerate kernel optimizations and delivery of private deployment features.
[00:02:27] Diego Alvarez: The KV cache experiments are high ROI for cost per token; without infra attention we risk higher unit costs.
[00:02:40] Speaker 6: (inaudible) can we commit to contractor help as a stopgap?
[00:02:47] Maya Chen: Yes we discussed contractors; Hannah, is contractor budget feasible?
[00:02:54] Hannah Lee: We can reallocate a one-off budget for 2 contractors for 3 months, but the full headcount needs approval for ongoing costs.

[00:03:10] Liam O'Connor: My bias is Bundle A but with a 30-day review clause. If we don't see throughput improvements in 6-8 weeks we can pivot hiring.
[00:03:25] Priya Sharma: I can scope ramp milestones tied to the review clause — bench, kernel selection outcomes, integration tests.
[00:03:35] Maya Chen: Okay provisional decision: move forward with Bundle A, conditional on engineering milestone plan and finance sign-off. Action: Maya to draft decision doc.

-- Dedicated pricing sensitivity --
[00:03:55] Liam O'Connor: Next, pricing. We ran a quick sensitivity showing unit economics for Dedicated at 3 pricing tiers, factoring in reserved capacity and burst costs.
[00:04:12] Diego Alvarez: The main variance is utilization — at 40% utilization unit cost skyrockets; at 75% it's healthy. We need to be conservative.
[00:04:25] Hannah Lee: Finance recommends modeling 50% baseline utilization for planning. We should also flag churn scenarios.
[00:04:36] Priya Sharma: From infra side, autoscaling policies and burst-to-hosted fallbacks can reduce tail spend. But that adds complexity for customers.
[00:04:48] Maya Chen: Competition note: VectorCloud recently announced an 'always-on' reserved plan with aggressive price points, which puts pressure on our positioning.
[00:04:59] Liam O'Connor: We can differentiate on predictable SLOs and strong observability — charge a premium for SLA-backed capacity.
[00:05:12] Hannah Lee: Recommend three SKU lines: Starter (low commitment), Professional (mid), Enterprise (SLA, private). We'll run price elasticity experiments.
[00:05:26] Diego Alvarez: Action here: Priya to run cost matrix for 3 SKUs with worst-case utilization.

-- Latency SLO targets and benchmark plan --
[00:05:38] Liam O'Connor: We need to finalize new latency SLOs for our hosted API and Dedicated. Proposal: p95 < 250ms for hosted small models, p95 < 350ms for dedicated mixed workloads.
[00:05:55] Priya Sharma: Those numbers are aggressive for longer context lengths; we should tie SLOs to profile buckets (short chat, long completion, embeddings).
[00:06:07] Diego Alvarez: Also include quantization fallbacks; some kernels degrade output quality. Benchmarks must include both latency and output fidelity.
[00:06:18] Maya Chen: Let's do a two-week benchmark window: SE to run synthetic and real customer traces, research to validate output quality, product to catalog tradeoffs.
[00:06:30] Priya Sharma: I'll own the benchmark harness, Diego will own evaluation metrics, Liam will pull real traces.
[00:06:42] Liam O'Connor: Timeline: start 2026-06-01, finish 2026-06-14, report 2026-06-16.

[00:07:00] Speaker 3: (mumbling) question about KV cache invalidation patterns...
[00:07:08] Diego Alvarez: We'll include cache eviction scenarios in the benchmarks. Good catch.

-- Audit / Private deployment timeline --
[00:07:25] Maya Chen: Next topic: SOC 2 re-certification and Private deployment readiness. Where are we on docs and infra?
[00:07:35] Priya Sharma: Private deployment stack is feature-complete but needs hardened installer and KMS integrations. Estimated 8-10 weeks for customer-ready packaging if we prioritize.
[00:07:49] Hannah Lee: SOC 2 timeline is aligned with that; auditors want documented RBAC flows and KMS proof. We should schedule the dry run.
[00:07:59] Liam O'Connor: Can Legal and Security join the next deep-dive? We should bring in Compliance to close gaps.
[00:08:08] Maya Chen: Yes, next deep-dive with Security and Legal. Action: Liam to schedule compliance deep-dive.

-- Open Q&A / cross-functional risks --
[00:08:20] Maya Chen: Open floor for quick risks.
[00:08:25] Diego Alvarez: Risk: model drift in evals after quantization — need continuous evals.
[00:08:32] Priya Sharma: Risk: platform lock when customers choose private; need clear rollback and upgrade paths.
[00:08:40] Hannah Lee: Finance risk: if Dedicated adoption low, reserved capacity cost will underutilize; we should model convertible SKUs.

[00:08:55] Speaker 4: (voice) can you repeat the hiring decision?
[00:08:59] Maya Chen: Provisional Bundle A: 2 infra, 1 SE, 1 PM. Contingent on milestone plan and finance sign-off.

-- Recap / decisions --
[00:09:10] Maya Chen: Quick recap: 1) Approve provisional Bundle A hiring with 30-day review. 2) Run pricing sensitivity for Dedicated; Priya will provide cost matrix. 3) Two-week benchmark window starting 2026-06-01 for latency SLOs. 4) Compliance deep-dive to be scheduled.
[00:09:30] Liam O'Connor: I'll own SLO proposals and gathering traces.
[00:09:36] Priya Sharma: I'll own benchmark harness and infra cost matrix.
[00:09:41] Hannah Lee: I'll sign off on contractor budget temporarily and run financial scenarios.
[00:09:47] Maya Chen: Great. We'll reconvene after reports are in. Next sync 2026-06-16 at 14:00 UTC.

-- Transcript continuation with more granular chatter to simulate full length (timestamps approximate) --
[00:10:05] Diego Alvarez: FYI, bench tooling might require small infra spin to simulate tail latencies; that's included in Priya's work.
[00:10:18] Priya Sharma: Noted, will allocate a test cluster.
[00:10:33] Liam O'Connor: Question from #product slack — are we still planning the console changes for per-model tracing in Q3?
[00:10:42] Maya Chen: Yes Q3 but lower priority than Dedicated launch items. We can surface a minimal tracing view earlier.
[00:11:00] Speaker 7: (inaudible) is there a written tradeoff doc for quantization?
[00:11:06] Diego Alvarez: We'll publish a tech note post-benchmark. It will show latency/quality curves per quantization path.
[00:11:17] Priya Sharma: Also, can we align on allowed model contexts for Dedicated? There's customer ask for 32k contexts. That's a big perf hit.
[00:11:28] Liam O'Connor: Propose we tier context windows in SKUs — allow 32k for Enterprise only.
[00:11:37] Maya Chen: That aligns with pricing. Hannah?
[00:11:40] Hannah Lee: Yep Enterprise pricing can absorb that.

[00:11:55] Maya Chen: Any final comments?
[00:11:58] Speaker 2: thumbs up
[00:12:02] Maya Chen: Cool. Thanks everyone — action items and doc will be circulated. Meeting adjourned.
